What was the power achieved by Lord Buddha, Sankaracharya, the Prophet, and Jesus Christ? Can any political philosopher stand before those supreme powers? Can they even approach their capabilities? What profound changes have been brought about in human society by Buddha, the very embodiment of compassion, and by Sri Sankara, who provided guidance by evaluating the scriptures and the *Upanishads*? Has anyone else here been able to accomplish even a small fraction of their work? For that matter, could any prominent political figure ever surpass the path laid down by Sree Narayana Guru—who, having mastered the essence of Vedanta, guided the masses around him onto the right path through the avenue of faith—or by Sree Chattampi Swamikal, who awakened the people by exposing the Vedic practices that had lost their foundation over the course of time? Everyone knows that the answer is no.

What guided those noble sages there was a unique power rooted in tradition. Our people were ready to perceive it and accept them. Initially, they all had to face hardships. They had to practice immense sacrifice. Yet, with unfaltering steps, those great souls advanced, bearing witness to that unearthly radiance.

The essence, therefore, is that a great power guides us. We are moving along the path that has been illuminated for us. By treading this path rooted in tradition, we achieve only elevation. What we must possess is an inner thirst to discover it. It is for this that the youth of today must strive. Only then will your next generation step into a life of happiness and contentment.

This should not be interpreted to mean that I reject progressive ideologies. Why cannot we aspire for progress while remaining firmly rooted in our tradition? It appears that many today harbor misconceptions—believing that our ancient *Arsha Bharata* culture consists merely of outdated systems and must be entirely replaced. That is the mindset we need to change. If we change it, we can build a novel stream of thought in our cultural sphere. You can realize this even without my stating it. It is imperative that the cultural realm achieves elevation. Only then can a large section of the people be guided onto the right path. We have already seen that such modernization has occurred across various eras. Its movements continue to evolve. It is just that when it becomes outdated, there is a need to create a sense of novelty once again.

As previously mentioned, the problems of materialistic life constantly afflict us. How can a solution be found for this? How can we confront this calamity that stares everyone in the face? This is a thought that many might raise. To this, there is only one thing to say. Provide peace to your mind, which is the epicenter of all problems. Grant it tranquility. If you can provide that peace, the problems are resolved. No matter how severe they may be, you will realize that their intensity is gradually diminishing. Thus, the problems will be solved in due course.

How does one provide peace to the mind? That is where the contradictions between concepts reside. How can a mind that is boiling over and ready to explode be restrained? There have been numerous instances where it has been successfully restrained. We observe that there is a power in this world that transcends our human strength. We must believe in that power. Only if we believe can we truly discover it. The radiance of that power has been visible since the dawn of humanity. Since then, humans have begun to worship that power. That worship continues today. And it will endure as long as humanity exists.

We are moving forward through the light shown by those lives. Even though humans have progressed immensely, they are unable to distance themselves from that power—such is the magnitude of that power. That is God. We visualize that governing force in our minds. We present our problems to it. It compels us to live as rational and wise beings.

It is true that this power has been divided into various factions. They were named religions. The essence of all these religions is fundamentally the same: to achieve peace, harmony, and fulfillment in life through them. That is what all the *Vedas* and *Puranas* urge us to do.

As stated in the *Rig Veda*, let noble thoughts come to us from every side. Through them, lead a peaceful life. To achieve this, concentrate the mind. To attain concentration, worship that power consistently. It will instill courage in life. It will show the right path. Live according to that path. Let that be our ultimate goal.
Guru Vani
June 1977
Question: It is said that he is a realized soul (*Siddha*) and a wise one (*Jnani*). Then how did it remain unchanged?
Answer: There are certain residual karmic effects required to expel some ingrained tendencies (*Vasanas*). No matter how wise a person may be, it might not be efficacious for everyone.
Question: What is the reason it did not prove efficacious for him? Can you explain?

Answer: Some things can be explained, but not everything. A true devotee does not focus on destroying his vigor or preserving it like a precious jewel. Let whatever is meant to happen, happen. For him, devotion is the only refuge—thus, the glory of God is his sole sanctuary.
Question: Are you implying that figures like Bhogar and Narada are not genuine devotees?

Answer: Consider a father with ten children. They all address him as 'Father.' Their mother is also the same. The ten individuals act with ten distinct characteristics. Their innate inclination towards their father is identical. However, true love may only be evident in two or three of them. Only the father and mother can comprehend that; outsiders cannot. Similarly, there are those who practice Yoga through devotion. Some ritualists exhibit bodily purity and follow ritualistic practices according to Vedic traditions. A wise person observes all these with moderation and understands each individual's course of action. Regardless of the action performed, a devotee constantly perceives God alone as a sweet, pervasive presence.

Then, irrespective of the devotee's greatness, God behaves with them like an ignorant child, embodying the attitude, "I know nothing." At that time, God is consistently perceived acting within them, akin to a mother fondling an ignorant child. A karma yogi (ritualist) and a yogi might speak of their operational capabilities. They may discuss the specific qualities of medicine or the qualities of actions. God continuously fondles the devotee, much like a mother who does not allow her child to cry. A beloved child will eventually have to do certain things on their own. However, all are indeed children.
Question: Are you suggesting that a devotee lacks knowledge?
Answer: Does it imply that? It merely means they are at ease because they are devoid of the attitude of having acquired knowledge, or the ego of believing they are everything.
Question: Then, are you stating that Bhogar preserved his vitality by transmuting it into a bead using medicine?
Answer: Yes, it is preserved.
Question: At the Santhigiri Ashram, which propagates monotheism, certain framed pictures are worshipped. Is this appropriate?

Answer: Initially, humanity adopted various mediums to assign forms. All concepts prevailing to this day originated in this manner. Even the use of lamps is analogous. Meditation practices encompass numerous natures, such as formless meditation and meditation with form. The individuals who discovered these methods might have initiated a philosophical discipline—it may not be immediately comprehensible. Until one grasps it, by remaining steadfast and fixing upon it, and until the essence of other concepts is understood, if one stays firm in their belief, the mind's wavering will cease, and this can be discarded once the nature of wisdom dawns.
Question: A devotee was heard mentioning the term '*Trikalajnana*' to a friend. I wish to know more about *Trikalajnana*.

Answer: *Trikalajnana* is experienced by all individuals. It goes unnoticed simply because it is an unrecognized experience. Only the wise comprehend its true nature. Firstly, one must learn what its true form is. Subsequently, it can be known and understood.
Question: Why is the final phase of the lives of great souls fraught with sorrow?

Answer: Great souls do not attain greatness based on their physical constitution. The fundamental question is what they stood for. Recall the words of Manu. One should not ponder the origin and the fall of a river—similarly, do not contemplate the birth and death of great souls.
Question: It is considered that Monday is auspicious for prayer. Furthermore, prayers are conducted every month on the day of the full moon (*Pournami*). What is the rationale behind this?

Answer: It is a common belief among all people, not just ordinary Hindus, that Mondays and Thursdays are auspicious. Adherents of the *Shakteya* tradition consider Fridays and Tuesdays to be auspicious. For self-knowledge (*Atma Vidya*), Mondays and Thursdays are deemed auspicious across all religions. Sunday is also considered favorable. For sacrifice, Wednesdays and Saturdays are regarded as auspicious. This is calculated based on the spheres—specifically, planetary positions viewed as spheres. The planetary positions are determined based on the nine planets (*Navagrahas*). Days are deemed auspicious in reverence to the periods when they orbit and approach the earth.

The special significance attributed to the day of *Pournami* (full moon) stems from the division of a month into two lunar fortnights: the dark fortnight (*Karuthavavu*) and the bright fortnight (*Veluthavavu*). The bright fortnight culminates on the day the moon rises completely. The bright fortnight is characterized by the light directly transmitted from the solar sphere to the lunar sphere without any obstruction. Sages have deemed the *Pournami* vow auspicious based on the microscopic particles that reach the earth via the moonlight. These particles descend upon all animate and inanimate entities. This phenomenon gives rise to two distinct outcomes: firstly, it grants liberation to those who lead lives guided by *sattvic* thoughts, vows, and prayers; secondly, it is postulated that those engrossed in worldly thoughts on that day become entangled in worldly existence. It is based on this principle that the sages have instructed us that this day is conducive to prayer.
The Kulapathi speaks
July 1977
The Glory of Sacrifice
Beloved ones,

My aspiration to dedicate my life solely to virtuous deeds commenced during my early childhood. I must have been around seven years old at the time. I exhibited a profound interest in visiting temples for worship. You must not misconstrue my statement. This was an innate desire. Do you not possess similar innate inclinations? It is highly probable. Some individuals are predisposed to malevolent tendencies, ultimately culminating in their ruin. Simply put, I possessed an inherent obstinacy to avoid such a trajectory.

I began attending school. However, my focus was not on academics. I would incessantly ponder subjects related to devotion. A teacher inevitably noticed this characteristic. He inquired into the reasons behind my silence and unusual behavior. I could not refrain from telling him. My singular thought was that I must reach an ashram somehow. My family members raised objections. However, none of that deterred me. That childhood obstinacy ultimately led me to the Aluva Advaita Ashram. My pursuit of knowledge commenced there.

I gained substantial insight into ashram life during my time there. One crucial aspect—I had reached my destined location. That became my educational institution. My learning was to proceed from there. Subsequently, I arrived at Sivagiri. At Sivagiri, I resolved to establish a firm foundation for my endeavors. This is precisely what I intend to discuss. I can encapsulate it in a single word: sacrifice. After completing my own duties, I would fulfill the responsibilities of others as well. I never experienced any reluctance in doing so. This readiness for sacrifice became the defined objective of my life. I am articulating this specifically for the benefit of the younger generation. Cultivate this attitude during your formative years. If you do so, success is undoubtedly assured.

During this period, individuals from various regions would visit the ashram. I would readily offer them the necessary assistance. Consequently, they would naturally feel inclined to offer something in return to a child exhibiting such behavior. However, the moment I sensed they were about to offer monetary compensation, I would flee the premises. They would typically search for me precisely when they were preparing to depart. Yet, they would be unable to locate me anywhere. One could say this served as a form of amusement for me. I derived a sense of satisfaction from it.

At this juncture, I am reminded of another story about the greatness of sacrifice. It happened a long time ago, during the time of Chandragupta Maurya. A famous person from China arrived in India. He desired to meet and converse with everyone here. Accordingly, he got permission to meet Chanakya, the minister of Chandragupta. How would the minister of a great emperor live? The traveler pondered over it. When he reached near the minister's house one evening, he saw Chanakya sitting in a small hut near a small lamp, looking at the files of important problems of the country. He stood amazed. What kind of minister is this? Suddenly, Chanakya extinguished that lamp and lit another one. The prominent traveler could not help but ask why it was done. Chanakya said: "That belongs to the state, and this lamp is my own. Now we can talk."

The traveler could not help but respect the humility and sense of justice of the statesman named Chanakya. He went back to China with a great experience. What do we understand from this? Since those ancient times, our Indians were renowned for their humility, service, and righteousness. Their sacrifice highlighted the greatness of our country. It also provided an inspiration to be noticed all over the world.

Now another matter needs to be pointed out here. Each of us has different paths in life. We move forward accordingly. When seeing someone prosper, many people get jealous. That behavior pattern needs to be changed. It cannot be changed suddenly. For that, good thoughts must spread within us and wash away the impurities inside. Only then can it be said that one has lived as a human being, and only then will there be satisfaction. We have seen many people being dissatisfied and restless. Do you know the reason for that? Excessive greed. First, remove those greedy thoughts. That is why we must control our minds.

The goal of our life is realized when a systematic path is adopted. Some people set out to become monks while they still have all the obligations in life. Such monkhood is of no use to them. Those who are householders must fulfill their respective duties. Children must be raised through the right path. It is an essential factor for the progress of the country. When they grow up, they will find the ways for their employment on their own. Parents should prepare the paths for them to find it. And then, we should become proficient in activities for our peace of mind.

But there are some people. They lament over the future of their children. The pain of not being able to give them anything. Others, however, just earn money for their children. They amass unlimited wealth. I do not think there is a need for that either. If a son or daughter does not come through the path we intend, let them go their own way. There is no use in remembering that and lamenting over it. This life of ours is not for lamenting like that. We must live it completely.

We have to learn this matter by looking at the Westerners. We know how they raise their children and so on. They give the necessary instructions. They encourage them to do any job. There is no objection in that. Anyway, a job is a job. We cannot but respect it. Here, if someone has a little education, they are stubborn that they must get a job commensurate with it. Because of this, we can see countless youths who are jobless and do not do any work. They will experience the problems of life very seriously.

How can those who have thus become lazy by themselves be reformed? One can also see parents lamenting over it. What I have to say is that there is no point in that. Once the children reach a stage to stand on their own feet, the duty is fulfilled. After that, there is no wrong in even accepting monkhood. One's duty has been fulfilled. That is the path of a complete life.
Acquiring knowledge in childhood,
Seeking worldly enjoyments in youth,
Adopting a sage's conduct in old age,
And relinquishing the body in yogic bliss.

It is a necessity to acquire knowledge in childhood. Along with that, one must adhere to righteousness in life. Only then can a purification be built up even in later times. What is needed to maintain that discipline? Guidance! Instructions from a wise and mature Guru! That will provide immense solace. That will nurture the good tendencies within us. With that, a complete understanding of what Vanaprastha is and its full form will emerge within us. The knowledgeable ones say that it is the householders who can engage more in this matter. One can point out countless examples for that. The very fact that all the authors of the Puranas were householders is sufficient proof. That is the complete life. We must truly respect it.
Guru Vani
July 1977
Question: What could be the result of that preservation?
Answer: Some people say that Yoga disciplines state that if vigor is not lost, one will not suffer from old age and graying of hair, and will have a long life. It might be because of that.
Question: Even with these Yoga disciplines, if it does not calm down, then how can the mind be controlled?

Answer: The nature of controlling the mind when we face numerous sorrows - when we have no one to help us, or when a child dies, or when a husband dies - we often see women crying out loudly. It has been learned from them that when they repeat this for some time, their sorrow subsides, and within three months, the sorrow goes away. Similarly, one can surrender their sorrow by crying upon seeing a deity, a Guru, or a devotee who manifests divine light. Then he attains peace from that. A devotee who has none of this can pray and express his grievances to God by surrendering all his emotions with devotion. He attains peace from that.
Question: You did not finish explaining how women can fully experience devotion to God?

Answer: It is much easier for women than men to attain God through devotion. The proof for this are the wives of the Trinity, Satyavan Savitri, Arundhati, the women who lived with the sages, Anasuya, Priyamvada, Mary Magdalene whom you had deemed as the most fallen, Valli, Devayani, and if spoken of recent times, Sri Ramakrishna's wife, the disciples like Nivedita who came with Vivekananda, the Yogini who lived with Alathur Brahmananda - you are aware of such countless histories.
Question: That is correct. When you said it, each one seems correct. But despite seeing so much, all these stories are fading away from the people. Why would that be?

Answer: First, the changes in times brought about by the Chaturvarna system. Due to the changes that occurred over time for the Shudras and Vaishyas, it could not be passed on to the people. People only got to know the stories of some Siddhas or Yogis sitting somewhere and attaining name and fame. Such Siddhis and magical acts were mostly performed by Rajarshis. They have passed on many illusions to the people using money, knowledge, and wealth. Devaluing the deeds of ordinary devotees, poets and Rajarshis lined up behind them. Secondly, administrations changed in respective times, people of different religions ruled and brought their own religious customs, highlighting the malpractices of Hinduism and thereby covering up true devotion. They have also destroyed such historical records. Just as 'a tiger will eat grass if it has no other way', the scientific methods that came through them have instilled a business-style approach in us. Thus, the tradition of striving hard for worldly matters got ingrained in us.
Kulapathi Speaks
August 1977
Dear ones,

I had mentioned a few things about the greatness of sacrifice last time. However, what I have to say does not end there. There are many things I have gained from experience and understood by seeing and hearing. I have a strong desire to share them with you one by one. I feel that only then will you be able to understand its essence at least to some extent.

No matter how agonizing the problems I faced were, I tried to handle things with great equanimity. As a result, my problems were resolved. I can assert with certainty that there has never been a situation where they remained unresolved. To be more specific, I grew up in a desert. I did not collapse in its terrible heat. I moved forward every moment by gathering strength. Had I felt a little mental distress back then and given up everything, I would not have reached anywhere today. I would have been destroyed, entangled in the web of my own problems. Regardless, I do not know how I was able to gather such inner strength during those times.

Seeing this approach of mine, many well-wishers have given me various pieces of advice. They have tried to dissuade me from many of my actions. But even as I listened to all their advice, I continued to forge ahead on my own path. I want to clarify one thing here. We should not displease anyone. They might be saying such things with good intentions. However, accepting the good aspects of what they say while striving to find our own path is absolutely essential for success in life. We may perhaps not get its results very quickly. Even so, there is no doubt that the results will definitely be attained over time.

I started speaking about sacrifice. All the noble souls who have existed in the world have achieved sacrifice through their actions. Only they have been able to do something eternally lasting here. Look at the lives of great figures like Jesus Christ, Prophet Muhammad, and Buddha. You can find a vast abundance of sacrifice there. Why, were those lives not the very embodiment of sacrifice itself? We need not look elsewhere. Just take a look at Mahatma Gandhiji, who shines brightly as the apple of our India's eye. How incredibly magnificent is the message imparted by that life, which evolved through the greatness of sacrifice.

Was he not able to bring a superpower, which ruled over a vast nation, to its knees with a mere message of peace? I do not think anything like that has ever happened anywhere else in the world. Nor do I think such greatness could be achieved by anyone other than someone from India. Indians are people who have evolved through such a great deal of tolerance and tradition. Their life is one of friendship and peace. No power in the world has been able to surpass that.

Great souls have taken birth in this land of India in every era. Through their powerful sacrifices, they have bestowed vitality and life upon the entire human race. We must understand this clearly. That alone has endured, and that alone will endure in the future. Sree Narayana Guru is another great soul who brought about change to a certain extent through sacrifice. After Sree Sankara Bhagavatpada, it is difficult to find another Karma Yogi who brought about such a massive social revolution in our India. His supremely sacrificial life must be given its due value. If we can perform such a sacrifice or cultivate a discipline rich in sacrifice, there is no greater service than that.

This does not necessitate that we must rise to the level of those great souls. Their sacrifices attained a grand stature. Therefore, we need not be bewildered by the thought that we cannot even peek into that realm. It is through their relentless effort and readiness that they reached that supreme position. We should not retreat just by thinking about it. If we try to advance at least a little in that richness of sacrifice, we will receive its corresponding reward. The only thing is that its measure will be strictly in accordance with that sacrifice. Even so, there is no doubt that it will indeed culminate in success in life.

Then there is another aspect as well. Let me say that it is somewhat spiritual. It concerns the trajectory of our karma. Some people will not move forward no matter how hard they try, whereas some only need to try a little to reach their intended position. What is the reason for this? We can see many people feeling mentally pained thinking about it. One thing can be pointed out there. It is the variations in karma. One group of people might be striving in a state where the karmas or sacrifices performed in past lives are eagerly waiting for their completion. Thus, they achieve results very quickly. For others, the trajectory of karma might not have been completed in their past lives. There, this trajectory of karma can be completed only through sacrifice. Moreover, if we state the reason for soaring to great heights, it is because that person's very birth in this life is destined for it. They would have fulfilled all its aspects by performing sacrifices in their past lives itself. For such people, just a little effort is enough to attain it. So, one thing to remember is that the elevated position currently attained is the consequence of those good deeds practiced over multiple lifetimes.

The karmic trajectories of lifetimes take various forms. Many people do not seem to believe in it. It is good for us to remember one thing. If we take the different kinds of vicissitudes of life and analyze them, we will be convinced of that absolute truth. Many have to lead different kinds of lives. A blind child is born in the house of a rich man. In some places, children are born with stunted limbs. In other places, deformed births occur. We need to see and pay attention to all these things. What is all this? Is this not the resurrection of the cursed elements from past lives? How can we not believe these things? Thus, it implies that the baseness and good deeds of past lives follow us. There are many reasons why we emphasize this. And this is indeed something that others should reflect upon.
Now, let me say a little about the general life of human beings!

When a human being becomes sorrowful, they forget everything and wander around seeking refuge. In prosperity, they forget everything. That is a common trait. However, one must be able to cultivate a presence of mind that remains unshaken and unwavering under any circumstance. For that, they need to remember the Controller of this universe. They must act knowing that. Only then will sacrifice emerge in them. And only that will attain a permanent state.

All the great sacrificers the world has seen today are those who have worked unceasingly while standing behind that power. We can all clearly know what they have achieved as a result of it. People continue to follow their path. They find solace in it. Thus, their words inspire us to lead a contented life.

I spoke about the life of Jesus Christ earlier, didn't I? Was that life itself not offered up for the sake of sacrifice? What could be greater than that? Even in those final moments, he said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Do the words of that great man, who showcased that greatness by sacrificing even his own life, not echo everywhere even today? The case of the great Buddha is no different from this. Is he not the magnanimous soul who renounced all the royal pleasures of this world and set out for the welfare of the people? Who can lay claim to the magnificence of that sacrifice? How incredibly great have its achievements become! Thus, we can see that all the great souls who achieved immortality in life were the very embodiments of sacrifice.

Here, the foundation of our material life also requires such a sacrifice. If we wish to start any movement, that too requires sacrifice. The success of that institution will depend on the degree of this sacrifice. If we examine the lives of many people who have risen to prominence here today, we can understand this fact. But if the seeds of ego fall into their path of thought, we can see that not only the person but also the movement they built gets destroyed. So, when moving forward towards a goal through sacrifice, we must acquire all the knowledge related to it. What is that knowledge? What is it for? Ego dwells in the human mind. Therefore, the first thing needed is the removal of ignorance. Only that will lead to success. What is needed for that? We must understand the life perspectives of great people. We should think about it. Then, we must try to put it into practice. If we try step by step like this, we can reach our intended destination. That systematic life is, in a way, a sacrifice. We should strive for that. Perhaps many of you would like to know what its benefits are. Firstly, liberation from our karmic bonds. That leads to merging with God. Another is life's satisfaction. We will attain both of these. Through that, we will be led to the ethereal supreme state. What more does a human birth need than that?
Guruvani
August 1977
Question: How can one believe the stories of the Rajarshis recorded in these Puranas?

Answer: Currently, during the tenure of many rulers, some political enthusiasts often write histories to destroy the goodness of certain individuals. In this, we seem to have forgotten the national leaders who endured the sacrifices of holy souls. It appears to have been omitted from the histories written after attaining independence. The stories of contemporaries, fellow students, and colleagues are the ones that have been left out. And that too, in this democratic rule. Then is it any wonder if it was omitted by those who ruled in an absolute dictatorship?
Question: Looking at this experience, is it only the Rajarshis who have done so?

Answer: Not only among the Rajarshis, but also among common people and in the deity system, there are people who have attained direct realization and through it performed certain occult powers and magical feats. The shortcoming is that strong historical records could not be created for all of them. It was only through alliances at some administrative level, or through some other kind of knowledge or wealth, that it could be brought into a record. Those that have come through a true devotional nature are exceedingly rare.
Question: So, do you give importance only to devotion?
Answer: I do not give importance only to devotion like that. I am one who believes that everything has its own goodness in its respective measure.
Question: Isn't it easier to lead a family life in the path of devotion?
Answer: Yes. The path of devotion is the most suitable for family life.
Question: What is the reason for you to feel that nothing else is easy?

Answer: Practicing yoga techniques requires considerable time, and it involves certain changes in dietary habits depending on place and time. None of that may be convenient for family people. Therefore, there is quite a delay in carrying forward yoga practices. There are some ritualists who practice Vedic methods. They too have a specific time schedule for mantras and tantras. They will experience it as quite a delay.
Question: Then what about the state of a Jnani (wise one)?
Answer: The Jnani truly evaluates all these aspects. Viewing all these moderately, experiencing an inspiration from God, he moves forward acting on his own.
Guruvani
October 1977
Question: Some Vedantins are heard saying this, aren't they? I am not born, I do not die, there are no births and deaths in the world, the universe is an illusion. What is the reason?

Answer: Vedanta is correct. The reason Vedanta came to be is because there was something else, isn't it? Those who said this universe is an illusion were living beings, weren't they? With the help of the five elements, with the help of the five senses, and thus with the help of the koshas (sheaths), the soul, which is enclosed in this body within a form created by God, ranging from the nature of the annamaya kosha to the anandamaya kosha, is brought through the jnanamaya kosha to the vijnanamaya kosha. Thus, the whole world can know only through this. When the knowledge that comes in this way turns one into a subtle thinker, it is often called jnana thought, vijnana thought, and ajnana thought. Based on this, some experience it in the formed, the formless, and the undivided.
Question: These Siddhas are assumed to be Jnanis, aren't they? Then what made you distinguish between Siddhas and Jnanis?

Answer: Siddhi and Jnana are indeed two different things. Siddhi utilizes certain mantras and tantras, worshiping through certain deity systems or Yogishwara systems, experiencing it, and creating some minor experiences among the people - acting like the nature of a yogi or a deity oneself. A Jnani does not do this. Through the path originating from the Guru's teaching, recognizing everything that can come into the light, even realizing what sustenance of life or sustenance of prana is, the Guru's teaching is an instrumental path capable of perceiving even the unique virtue of those koshas in which that prana operates. But a Siddha is not like that; a Siddha proceeds by believing only the words received from the guidance he prefers. There is only a very distant relationship between a Siddha and a Jnani.
Question: You mentioned the Guru's teaching. He comes forward by giving the form of some favorite deity like this, doesn't he?

Answer: That is correct. We can record it here like an administration. The peons standing near the king are also called peons. In courts, every bench clerk has peons. Likewise, there are some in certain companies. There are peons in all offices and schools. Village officers have peons. But the status and privileges enjoyed by a peon who can meet the king and discuss matters may not be found among these peons or superior officers. Similarly, one practices yoga, one practices Guruhood. It exists in many states and many justifications. All this exists through justification as well. Certain shifts in position are the reason for this.
Guruvani
November 1977
Question: So, what should be understood from this is that the Gurus you speak of themselves exist in numerous natures like this, and their states themselves exist in various ways, right?
Answer: Yes.
Question: If so, what kind of Gurus should actually lead this?
Answer: Gurus of all kinds can show the reality. But that is solely dependent on their growth.
Question: Are you referring to the growth in the path of each one, or the overall growth?
Answer: There are Gurus who reach reality through the growth of each one. There are also Gurus who reach reality by seeing it as a whole.
Question: You said that there are Gurus who reach through the growth of each one. How is that?

Answer: A devotee is a traveler of a path. A yogi is a traveler of a path. A karma yogi is a traveler of a path. The Jnani, who grows by bringing all these together, is a visionary. There are also Gurus born at the beginning and end of yugas (epochs). The names of the Gurus concerning the yugas are Avatara Purushas (incarnations). They will also have some special characteristics.
Question: What would those special characteristics be?

Answer: We have seen some historical records, haven't we? Sree Rama, Sree Krishna, and Balarama were all born in different eras. Among them, Sree Rama was born in the Treta Yuga and showed many special characteristics. But none of the previously mentioned ones were able to show such great special characteristics as Sree Krishna.
Question: What could be the reason for that?

Answer: When changes in the epochs (yugas) occur, certain specific changes will also be seen in the prominent figures (Yugapurushas) born in those respective epochs. A Chaturyuga is completed by four yugas. Therefore, the gurus born at the beginning and end of that epoch will possess greater capabilities. The authorities of this Chaturyuga are the Manus.
Question: What is your opinion regarding the authority of individuals like Sri Krishna in this context?
Answer: Sri Krishna is the final guru of the Dwapara Yuga and the first guru of the Kali Yuga.
Question: What is the reason for you to state both together?

Answer: Sri Krishna has exhibited many independent actions. His glory will continue to be reflected to some extent until the final phase of this Kali Yuga. That is what stems from that independence. It is not mere independence; rather, whatever is necessary emerges appropriately at that very moment. If one examines the lives of other incarnations (Avataras), the concept of acting 'according to command' can be observed. However, Sri Krishna operated entirely independently. The names of the gurus and incarnations who have appeared thus far continue to be repeated. Yet, in practical application and in the enthusiasm of the people, is it not Sri Krishna who is seen at the forefront?
Question: What is the reason for this independence being reflected in Sri Krishna?

Answer: When referring to Kali, does it not evoke the impression of doing anything with an independent nature? Yes, it does. If one closely observes Sri Krishna, it becomes evident that, like a primordial trait, he reinforced that independence and the outdated historical records right at its inception. Similarly, he led his life in a manner that suggested the impending future would possess distinctive characteristics. Next is the nature of the visionaries belonging to the lineage of the aforementioned Manus. They acquired knowledge over long periods and documented certain teachings and guidelines. Through this, profound foresight is also seen to flourish. However, the sages (Rishis) who evolve within the lineage of the incarnations continue certain hymns and traditions of service. They demonstrate various practices of mystical powers (Siddhis). The realized souls (Jnanis) who grow in the lineage of Manu merely advise and disseminate knowledge suitable for their respective times. There are Siddhas and Jnanis who fail to recognize this distinction. They often criticize various matters, offer advice, and depart. It is merely akin to certain Vedantins attempting to portray themselves as Jnanis by quoting the words of the realized ones without possessing any experiential knowledge. The majority of the Jnanis we encounter on this earth are those who flaunt their erudition by solely consolidating the maxim, 'Brahma Satyam, Jagan Mithya' (Brahman is the truth, the world is an illusion).

For a true Jnani, knowledge means self-knowledge (Atma Vidya). It is that which self-illuminates within one's own soul. Such Jnanis are the true assets we possess. For instance, consider the science of Ayurveda. Similarly, Mantra Vidya, Tantra Vidya, and Shastra Vidya. If one were to examine each of these individually, they would appear as the ultimate truth. It is through these disciplines that we practically comprehend the documented experiences of the great sages and a select few ascetics.
Guruvani
December 1977
Question: Why did you differentiate between the great sages (Rishis) and the ascetics (Sanyasis)?

Answer: The great sages are those who attain experiential knowledge and document everything in a manner that is highly beneficial to the common people, while also demonstrating its practical application. Only a few among the ascetics acknowledge this. They remain aloof from everything. They maintain no attachments and possess a sense of complete detachment towards all things. They merely exhibit certain imitative behaviors solely for the purpose of sustenance.
Question: So, is it not about such ascetics that our people have been speaking?

Answer: Yes, people simply amuse themselves by recounting tales of those who practice certain yoga disciplines and survive without even needing dry leaves or plain water. They waste their time unnecessarily discussing these stories without any understanding of how useful this is to the public or how people can attain such states. Some individuals, tempted by the intensity of mystical powers (Siddhis) and erudition, waste their time praising them. A true Jnani is one who respects these various aspects by assigning them their appropriate value. This Jnani evaluates everything, demonstrates the validity of all paths to the people, and attempts to impart knowledge by giving it a distinct character.
Question: What exactly did you mean by the distinct character of knowledge?

Answer: By documenting that specific events occurred in certain periods, they perceive only the unadulterated truth within the nature of the Jnanis, and they eventually convince us that there is only one ultimate truth.
Question: You mentioned the Manus earlier. In what context are you referring to them?

Answer: The Manus are the ones who encompass all the descriptions of the world. Upon closer examination, they are the absolute authorities governing creation, preservation, and destruction. The governance of this world is characterized by fourteen Manus leading up to the great deluge (Pralaya). Such great souls have recorded that the duration of each Manu consists of seventy-one Chaturyugas. If their guidance falters, and if the world strays, it will be plunged into perpetual blindness. Until a specific birth occurs to rectify it, the world will have to continue traveling on that misguided path.
Question: Has any of the Manus ever made such a mistake?
Answer: Yes. We shall discuss that later.
Question: What types of worship practices do you think are most desirable to adopt during this period?
Answer: Four modes of worship practices are considered the most ideal.
Question: Which are they?

Answer: Karma, Yoga, Jnana, and Bhakti. It is difficult for Karma and Yoga to be fully reflected in this era. The Karma Yoga spoken of by an ascetic is different. An ascetic considers any action undertaken as Karma. Ordinary people perform actions adhering to certain rules and regulations. This cannot be effectively mirrored in current times. Similarly, Yoga also poses difficulties for common people. Jnana can be manifested in any era. Even if not manifested, nothing else can affect Jnana. Bhakti holds significance in all times. Nothing can reach completion without devotion. Particularly, Bhakti is the most suitable path in this age.

Question: Since you mentioned that Bhakti is the most beneficial in this era, would you be willing to explain how one should practice this devotion, and how it can remain effective from the beginning, through the middle, and until the end of time?

Answer: Initially, learn to practice all the disciplines of a devotee to the point of turning them into experiential nature. Even if we attain a minor spiritual experience in such a manner, the assistance of a Guru in the absolute nature of devotion is required in every way to gain clarity over it. Regardless of whatever flaws may exist in that Guru's conduct, the one who believes will be able to find a way to derive spiritual satisfaction from it.
Question: What do you mean by stating "regardless of whatever flaws"? Can there be various types of flaws like that?

Answer: There are flaws in many ways. When a person practices devotion, if the knowledge attained is not complete or accompanied by humility, an arrogance will arise regarding the knowledge itself. It is specifically termed as 'Satvik Ahankara' (righteous ego). You are all well aware of the consequences that follow when arrogance takes root!
Guruvani
